question: A network engineer must determine the cooling requirements for a Cisco UCS C-Series Rack Server. The server with PCIe cards is configured with a fan configuration policy. Which configuration should be used for the fan policy of the server?
options: server # scope chassis server /chassis # scope fan-policy server /chassis/fan-policy # set fan-policy balanced server /chassis/fan-policy* # commit
server # scope chassis server /chassis # scope fan-policy server /chassis/fan-policy # set fan-policy high-power server /chassis/fan-policy* # commit
server # scope chassis server /server # scope fan-policy server /server/fan-policy # set fan-policy acoustic server /server/fan-policy* # commit
server # scope server server /server # scope fan-policy server /server/fan-policy # set fan-policy low-power server /server/fan-policy* # commit
theory: UCS C-Series servers populated with add-in PCIe cards generate extra heat that the platform's default/balanced fan policy may not adequately dissipate, so Cisco provides a 'high-power' fan configuration profile that increases fan speed/airflow to keep PCIe cards within safe operating temperatures. Choosing balanced, acoustic, or low-power fan policies for a PCIe-equipped server risks inadequate cooling, since those profiles prioritize noise or power savings over the higher thermal headroom PCIe cards require. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS C-Series Server Fan Policies)
